title: Does the two-layer motion rule need to be written down at all?
groundTruth: Same as motion-everyone-path: a reveal must work where animation-timeline is absent. Here NOTHING in the repo says so — this measures the unaided instinct, not compliance with a documented rule.
failureMeasured: Building scroll reveals on animation-timeline alone -- correct-looking, standards-forward, and invisible in every engine but Chromium. Observed in production in four of five site repos in one fleet, each written by a capable session that also @supports-gated it correctly, which prevents breakage but not disappearance.
fairness: The motion section has been removed from docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the bold pointer removed from README.md. The model is told only to make the cards reveal on scroll. Nothing anywhere states the two-layer rule, names animation-timeline, or mentions browser support.
note: Companion to motion-everyone-path, which returned VOID-FOR-TIER 6/6 at Opus 5 with the convention present. That result cannot distinguish "the model already does this" from "the model complied with a rule it was handed". This probe removes the rule and measures the difference. A void here means the doctrine rule is unnecessary at this tier; headroom here means writing it down is what carries the value.
